metadata.title: Client & Program Goals
metadata.purpose: Reference file for fitness programming and Claude Code integration

onboarding_goal_crosswalk.description: Maps the 4 onboarding goal selections to the full primary_goals list. Claude reads this first to know which goal IDs to activate.

fat_loss.secondary_consideration: If client is intermediate+ and protein-aware, consider ID 3 (Body Recomp) instead
fat_loss.notes: Default to ID 1. Upgrade to ID 3 only if experience=intermediate or advanced AND protein_awareness=intentional

muscle_gain.secondary_consideration: If client also wants fat loss and is intermediate+, layer ID 3 (Body Recomp)
muscle_gain.notes: Default to ID 2 for pure hypertrophy. ID 3 for simultaneous fat loss.

performance.secondary_consideration: Use ID 4 for strength-focused, ID 5 for sport/athleticism-focused. Check goal_detail from onboarding to decide.
performance.notes: If goal_detail mentions a sport or event → ID 5. If it mentions lifting numbers or strength → ID 4.

general_health.secondary_consideration: ID 7 for most clients. ID 9 if age 55+. ID 10 if motivation_style=feeling_energy and stress=high or very_high.
general_health.notes: General health clients benefit most from functional movement and mind-body integration layers.

special_population_flags.description: These override the above if present in client profile
special_population_flags.prenatal: If client notes pregnancy in injuries or current_physical_state → activate ID 11. Require OB clearance note.
special_population_flags.postpartum: If client notes recent childbirth → activate ID 8. Require medical clearance note.
special_population_flags.active_aging: If age >= 55 → layer ID 9 considerations regardless of primary goal

instructions_for_claude.step_1: Read onboarding_goal_crosswalk to identify which primary_goal_ids to activate based on client's selected goal
instructions_for_claude.step_2: Check special_population_flags — these override everything if triggered
instructions_for_claude.step_3: Identify Secondary Goals from client profile and layer modifications on top
instructions_for_claude.step_4: Apply new_onboarding_field_integrations to adjust coaching language and programming per client's motivation_style, struggle_style, mobility_limitations, and body_awareness
instructions_for_claude.step_5: Check for contraindications and cross-reference injury_navigation.json if injuries field is non-empty
instructions_for_claude.step_6: Output program structured by session, week, and phase

new_onboarding_field_integrations.description: How the new onboarding fields (steps 5, 8, 9, 10, 15) modify goal programming and coaching approach

performance_data.program_notes_tone: Lead with metrics. Frame every session in terms of output — weight moved, reps completed, time under tension.
performance_data.progress_framing: Week-over-week numbers. PR tracking. Quantified milestones.

feeling_energy.program_notes_tone: Lead with identity and sensation. Frame sessions around how they will feel — strong, aligned, energized.
feeling_energy.progress_framing: Energy improvements, confidence shifts, how clothes fit, mood changes.

both.program_notes_tone: Alternate — metrics one week, feeling-based the next. Both lanes matter.

reminder_why.coaching_trigger: When client misses sessions or checks in low — pull their vision and identity_statement from onboarding. Reconnect before adjusting program.
reminder_why.language: Reference Kim's system prompt affirmation language. 'You told me you wanted to feel ___. That version of you is still here.'

simplify.coaching_trigger: When struggling — immediately reduce program to 1 exercise, 1 set, just show up.
simplify.language: No big picture. One thing. Today only.

accountability.coaching_trigger: Direct check-in. Name the pattern without shame. Hold the standard.
accountability.language: Firm warmth. 'We said ___ days this week. What happened? Let's fix it together.'

space.coaching_trigger: Acknowledge and step back. No pressure check-in. Let client lead return.
space.language: 'I'm here when you're ready. No judgment. Just come back.'

mobility_limitations.description: Layer mobility modifications on top of goal programming. Cross-reference client_assessment_schema.json for specific exercise substitutions.
mobility_limitations.tight_hips: Add hip mobility to every warm-up. Substitute squat patterns as needed.
mobility_limitations.limited_shoulder: Modify all overhead and pressing work. Add shoulder mobility to warm-up.
mobility_limitations.ankle_restriction: Heel elevation on squats. Add ankle mobility drills.
mobility_limitations.thoracic_stiffness: Add thoracic extension to warm-up. Cue bracing on pressing.
mobility_limitations.hamstring_tightness: Limit hinge range initially. Add hamstring work post-session.
mobility_limitations.wrist_discomfort: Neutral grip alternatives. Wrist warm-up mandatory.

body_awareness.low: Include mind-muscle cues in every exercise description. Recommend lighter load to establish connection. Reference mind_muscle_connection.json.
body_awareness.moderate: Standard cues. Reinforce connection on isolation work.
body_awareness.high: Minimal cueing. Can introduce advanced techniques — pause reps, slow eccentrics, blood flow restriction.

recent_training_and_frequency.description: Adjusts starting volume regardless of stated experience level
recent_training_and_frequency.rarely_or_nothing: Start at 60% of target volume. Build over 2 weeks.
recent_training_and_frequency.5x_plus: Can push to upper range of target volume from week 1.

not_tracking_protein.program_note: Gently surface protein importance in week 1 program notes. Simple — not prescriptive. 'Fueling well supports your recovery and results.'

low_meal_frequency_high_volume.flag: If meal_frequency=1-2 AND days_per_week >= 4 → flag energy availability concern in program notes. Suggest eating before training.

identity_statement.description: The single most powerful coaching tool in the profile. Pull client's own words.
use_when: Client expresses doubt or wants to quit
At start of each new program phase
identity_statement.how: Quote directly. 'You told me that the version of you who is consistent is someone who [identity_statement]. That person is still you.'

primary_goals.name: Fat Loss
primary_goals.definition: Reducing overall body fat percentage while preserving as much lean muscle as possible

primary_goals.name: Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy)
primary_goals.definition: Increasing muscle size through progressive overload and sufficient volume

primary_goals.name: Body Recomposition
primary_goals.definition: Simultaneously reducing body fat and building lean muscle — typically for intermediate+ clients
programming_priorities: Balanced fat loss and hypertrophy stimulus

primary_goals.name: Strength & Power
primary_goals.definition: Maximizing force production for maximal strength or explosive power output

primary_goals.name: Athletic Performance
primary_goals.definition: Improving sport-specific physical qualities — speed, agility, power, coordination, endurance
primary_goals.rest_periods: Full recovery for power/speed; short for conditioning

primary_goals.name: Cardio & Endurance
primary_goals.definition: Building aerobic capacity, cardiovascular efficiency, and stamina for sustained effort
primary_goals.rest_periods: Active or full depending on zone

primary_goals.name: Functional Fitness
primary_goals.definition: Improving movement quality, coordination, and strength for real-life tasks and daily activities

primary_goals.name: Postpartum Recovery & Enhancement
primary_goals.definition: Supporting the physical recovery and return to training after childbirth
special_considerations: Always confirm medical clearance before programming
Flag any symptoms (leaking, prolapse, pain) — refer out immediately
Do not progress load until foundational core and pelvic floor are established

primary_goals.name: Active Aging
primary_goals.definition: Maintaining and improving strength, mobility, balance, and independence for clients 55+

primary_goals.name: Mind-Body Integration
primary_goals.definition: Training that emphasizes the connection between mental and physical wellness — breathwork, mobility, mindfulness in movement

primary_goals.name: Prenatal Fitness
primary_goals.definition: Safe, trimester-aware exercise programming for pregnant clients
programming_priorities: Baby and mother safety above all
special_considerations: Always confirm OB clearance before programming
Avoid supine position after first trimester

secondary_goals.name: Injury Navigation
secondary_goals.description: Client has a current or past injury limiting movement
secondary_goals.programming_impact: Modify exercises, avoid loaded ranges, cross-reference injury_navigation.json

secondary_goals.name: Mobility & Flexibility
secondary_goals.description: Client wants to improve range of motion
secondary_goals.programming_impact: Add warm-up and cooldown mobility work, prioritize joint prep

secondary_goals.name: Stress & Recovery
secondary_goals.programming_impact: Reduce intensity, prioritize parasympathetic training, shorter sessions

secondary_goals.name: Confidence Building
secondary_goals.description: New to training, needs wins and momentum
secondary_goals.programming_impact: Lower complexity, higher success rate exercises, celebrate progression

secondary_goals.name: Competition Prep
secondary_goals.description: Client is preparing for an event or competition
secondary_goals.programming_impact: Peak programming, taper planning, sport-specific final phase

secondary_goals.name: Weight Maintenance
secondary_goals.description: Client is at goal weight and wants to sustain
secondary_goals.programming_impact: Balanced stimulus, no aggressive cut or bulk

secondary_goals.name: Postural Correction
secondary_goals.description: Client has imbalances such as anterior pelvic tilt or rounded shoulders
